A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original TOFU, MUSE and WMDP experiments, probability-dynamics analyses, qualitative examples, ablations and training-time measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds probability-dynamics results for BS-T and BS-S in Figure 4a–b.

M1.justification: v2 Sections 4.2 and 5.2 introduce an optional off-policy BS-S variant that samples auxiliary responses once and keeps them fixed, whereas v1 Algorithm 2 resamples during training. The core losses and implemented on-policy pseudocode remain unchanged; no experimental switch to the new variant is reported.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same TOFU tasks, MUSE-News and MUSE-Books, WMDP-Bio/Cyber and MMLU retention coverage. Moving MUSE-News to Appendix F.3 does not remove coverage, and the added dynamics plots introduce no distinct task or environment.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain the same methods: GradDiff, NPO, RMU, SimNPO and WGA where previously included. MUSE-Books still omits NPO. Original/retrain references and the additional UNDIAL and GRU timing comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: The reported splits, model configurations, metrics, training schedules and hyperparameter searches match across versions, particularly Appendix E. The added BS-T/BS-S plots extend the existing log-probability-versus-epoch diagnostic without documenting a different evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 4a–b extends the squeezing-effect analysis to BS-T and BS-S, testing whether they suppress target responses and high-likelihood alternatives during training. v1 showed these dynamics only for GA and NPO. Existing hyperparameter analyses, loss ablations and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: The statistical reporting practices remain unchanged. v2 adds no seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or specified uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: New Figure 4a–b reports decreasing target and high-likelihood-region log-probabilities under BS-T and BS-S. The matched benchmark tables, LaaJ bar values, hyperparameter heatmaps, loss-ablation scores and timing measurements remain unchanged, including the relocated MUSE-News results.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained AKG lemma and GA/BS-T residual theorem, v2 adds Theorem 5.3 and its Appendix D.3 proof for kernel-weighted residual aggregation in off-policy BS-S. Appendix D.4 additionally formulates an on-policy objective and derives its score-function gradient term, substantially extending the formal analysis and its stated boundaries.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens the claimed theoretical contribution from explaining BS-T to explaining BS more generally, accompanying the added off-policy BS-S analysis. The central claims about spurious unlearning, belief-based suppression and the forgetting–retention trade-off remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets off-policy BS-S as distributing forgetting pressure across kernel-weighted continuations, producing smoother updates. It also explicitly explains why its analysis excludes the implemented on-policy variant. However, Appendix G retains v1's broader statement that BS-S lacks a formal treatment, leaving an inconsistency.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 states that the code has been merged into OpenUnlearning and provides a link. v2 also explicitly identifies the implementation as on-policy. Hardware, software versions, training configurations and hyperparameter-search information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations throughout the introduction and appendices, including Liao et al. (2026), AEGIS, and brief related-work additions on multitask and graph unlearning. These expand the bibliography and context without substantially changing the paper's positioning relative to prior unlearning methods.

P1.justification: Theory moves from Section 4.2 into a standalone Section 5, and method motivation and algorithms receive separate subsections. MUSE discussion and the LLM-use statement are relocated; terminology, affiliations and publication information are updated. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially reorganized: Figure 4 becomes a three-panel display, Figure 1 is graphically revised, and Figure 3 becomes smaller and text-wrapped. WMDP, MUSE and loss-ablation tables adopt compact wrapped layouts; MUSE-News moves to Appendix F.3. These are display changes beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: The added BS-T/BS-S dynamics plots directly strengthen the empirical support for the proposed mechanism, and v2 reports code integration instead of only promising release. The new off-policy theorem expands analytical coverage, but does not cover the implemented on-policy method. Its value is also limited by the retained residual-sign inconsistency in Appendix D.2 and the stale BS-S limitation in Appendix G. Overall, the revision provides useful but bounded improvements.
